articles.title: Primavera Sound anuncia shows em SP antes de festival em Interlagos; veja atrações | G1
articles.standfirst: Nation of Language, Mannequin Pussy, Model/Actriz e outros artistas se apresentam nos dias 2, 3 e 4 de dezembro. Ingressos custam a partir de R$ 250.
articles.summary: Nation of Language, Mannequin Pussy, Model/Actriz e outros artistas se apresentam nos dias 2, 3 e 4 de dezembro. Ingressos custam a partir de R$ 250.
articles.body:
Underscores , Nation Of Language e Umru são anunciados no Primavera Cidade — Foto: Divulgação

Quem vai ao Primavera Sound São Paulo em dezembro poderá assistir a shows do festival antes mesmo de chegar a Interlagos. A organização anunciou nesta segunda-feira (19) a programação do primavera na Cidade, com apresentações nos dias 2, 3 e 4 de dezembro, no Cine Joia, na Liberdade, e na Audio, na Água Branca.

Os shows acontecem na semana do festival principal, marcado para os dias 5 e 6 de dezembro, no Autódromo de Interlagos. A proposta é levar parte da programação a casas de shows da cidade, em vez de concentrar todas as apresentações no local do evento.

Entre os artistas confirmados estão Nation of Language, Mannequin Pussy, Model/Actriz, Smerz e Ecco2k. A programação também inclui Metrika, Sophia Stel e uma apresentação conjunta de underscores e umru.

Local: Cine Joia — Praça Carlos Gomes, 82, Liberdade

Atrações: underscores b2b umru, Ecco2k, Sophia Stel e Metrika

Local: Audio — Avenida Francisco Matarazzo, 694, Água Branca, Zona Oeste

Atrações: Nation of Language e Mannequin Pussy

Local: Cine Joia — Praça Carlos Gomes, 82, Liberdade, Centro

Os ingressos serão vendidos pela plataforma Ingresse . Os valores do primeiro lote vão de R$ 250 a R$ 450, de acordo com o local e o setor.

No Cine Joia, os ingressos para a pista custam R$ 250 a inteira e R$ 125 a meia-entrada, tanto para os shows de 2 quanto para os de 4 de dezembro.

Na Audio, onde acontecem as apresentações de 3 de dezembro, a pista custa R$ 300 a inteira e R$ 150 a meia-entrada. No mezanino, os valores são de R$ 450 e R$ 225, respectivamente.

Quem comprou o passaporte do Primavera Sound terá acesso antecipado à retirada gratuita de ingressos entre as 10h de terça-feira (20) e as 10h de quarta-feira (21), limitado a dois ingressos por CPF e sujeito à disponibilidade. A venda para o público geral começa ao meio-dia de quarta-feira (21).

As compras on-line têm taxa de conveniência de 20% sobre o valor total. Quem preferir comprar presencialmente poderá ir à bilheteria oficial, na Rua Bela Cintra, 1966, no Jardim Paulista, de segunda a quinta-feira, das 13h às 17h, exceto feriados. Também haverá bilheteria física no Cine Joia e na Audio nos dias dos shows.

A classificação etária informada pela organização é de 16 anos. Menores de 5 anos não podem entrar. Crianças e adolescentes de 5 a 15 anos podem assistir às apresentações se estiverem acompanhados dos pais ou responsáveis legais, mediante apresentação de documento de identidade.

articles.title: Escola histórica de Jundiaí é cenário de nova série do Globoplay | G1
articles.standfirst: Escola Estadual Conde Parnaíba, localizada no Centro de Jundiaí, foi utilizada como cenário da história 'As Meninas da Garagem Secreta', que acompanha três estudantes que lidam com as descobertas e dilemas da pré-adolescência; produção estreia nesta segunda-feira (19).
articles.summary: "As Meninas da Garagem Secreta" estreia no Globoplay com trama gravada na Escola Conde do Parnaíba, em Jundiaí, sobre dilemas da pré-adolescência.
articles.body:
A cidade de Jundiaí (SP) foi escolhida para ser o cenário de uma série infantojuvenil que transformou a "Terra da Uva" na cidade fictícia "Venceslau Braga".

As gravações de "As meninas da Garagem Secreta" aconteceram durante o mês de fevereiro em alguns pontos turísticos de Jundiaí, como o Jardim Botânico, a Praça Marechal Floriano Peixoto (Praça do Coreto) e o Largo São Bento. Contudo, o prédio jundiaiense a receber mais destaque foi a Escola Estadual Conde do Parnaíba, transformada na escola das personagens principais da série de TV.

“As meninas da Garagem Secreta” é uma produção nacional da Mixer Films — Foto: Divulgação

O diretor geral da produção, João Daniel Tikhomiroff, disse ao g1 que a escolha pela cidade foi feita pensando carinhosamente nos detalhes da história que eles queriam contar.

"A gente buscou uma locação que tivesse essa característica da cidade de interior, tivesse um prédio da escola, a nossa grande protagonista... e encontramos em Jundiaí, não só a a cidade, mas tudo que tem em volta. O Colégio Conde da Parnaíba deu um charme muito especial para a série. Foi perfeito para contar essa história tão deliciosa como a das Meninas da Garagem Secreta" , afirmou.

Série ‘As Meninas da Garagem Secreta’ foi gravada dentro de escola de Jundiaí — Foto: Juan Ribeiro / Divulgação

Além dos ambientes, a produção contou também com a contratação de diversos profissionais locais para diferentes funções, como figuração e fornecedores de equipamentos e estrutura de apoio. No total, foram mais de 90 pessoas na equipe técnica.

🎞️ Uma série sobre inspiração e esperança

Baseada em uma ideia original da companhia teatral Cia. Delas, “As meninas da Garagem Secreta” conta a história de três meninas protagonistas que, por acaso, decidem criar um grupo secreto e contam com a adesão inesperada dos demais colegas de sala. O grupo também mobiliza todos ao seu redor com a apresentação de histórias de mulheres que as inspiram.

Série foi gravada em escola centenária de Jundiaí — Foto: Juan Ribeiro / Divulgação

Em uma sessão de estreia da série no sábado (17), em São Paulo (SP), Júlia Ianina, uma das roteiristas do projeto, destacou a mensagem que a série passa para os telespectadores.

"É uma série sobre amizade, sobre inspiração, sobre a relação entre pais, filhos, família. É uma série que me enche de esperança, e a gente precisa tanto de esperança, né? Então eu espero que ela inspire vocês também, que vocês se divirtam e partilhem com a gente essa alegria", afirmou.

🎥 Quem são 'As meninas da Garagem Secreta'?

Série infantojuvenil conta história de mulheres marcantes da ciência, da arte e da sociedade — Foto: Juan Ribeiro / Divulgação

Bárbara (Morena Machado), Sara (Mari Campolongo) e Carolina (Julia Rodrigues) são três alunas do sexto ano que fundam, por acaso, o Clube Secreto da Baderna.

A inspiração do clube vem de Maria Baderna, bailarina italiana que vivia no Rio de Janeiro e teve sua participação do Theatro Municipal banida por conta de suas inspirações em elementos não clássicos em sua dança. Para o grupo de artistas que passou a seguir a bailarina, deu-se o nome de “baderneiros”, termo então associado de modo pejorativo a bagunça e tumulto.

Atrizes Morena Machado, Mari Campolong e Julia Rodrigues caracterizadas como Bárbara, Sara e Carolina para série ‘As Meninas da Garagem Secreta’ — Foto: Juan Ribeiro / Divulgação

Reunidas na garagem da família de Sara, o trio cria uma linguagem divertida com música, memes, charadas e performances para dividir com os amigos da escola biografias de mulheres extraordinárias que a história tentou apagar.

Enquanto descobrem histórias marcantes de grandes nomes da ciência, da arte e da sociedade, as garotas enfrentam dilemas típicos da pré-adolescência, como a pressão por perfeição, o medo de não se encaixar e as transformações da amizade. A trama também destaca papel fundamental dessas trajetórias no amadurecimento do trio.

A série tem como criadoras Julia Ianina, Camila Raffanti e Thais Medeiros; diretor geral de João Daniel Tikhomiroff; direção de Pedro Jorge e Thais Medeiros; direção de produção de Adriana Marques; e produção executiva de Mylena Mandolessi.

A série estreia nesta segunda-feira (19), no canal de TV Gloob e, e também no streaming do Globoplay.

Gloob: Exibição de segunda a quinta-feira, de 19 a 29 de outubro, às 17h00.

Globoplay: Lançamento em duas partes, de 19 a 26 de outubro, aberto para não assinantes.

articles.title: Jorge Ben Jor celebra carreira inigualável com samba, festa e emoção para estádio lotado | G1
articles.standfirst: Em show para 51 mil pessoas, cantor tocou por mais de duas horas em SP, se emocionou e reuniu convidados como Samuel Rosa, Baby do Brasil, Rael e Edi Rock.
articles.summary: Em show para 51 mil pessoas, cantor tocou por mais de duas horas em SP, se emocionou e reuniu convidados como Samuel Rosa, Baby do Brasil, Rael e Edi Rock.
articles.body:
Jorge Ben Jor em show no Nubank Parque, em São Paulo, em 17 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Lais Moss

"Oitenta e sete anos?!", era a exclamação que mais se ouvia neste sábado (17), durante o show de Jorge Ben Jor no Nubank Parque, em São Paulo. Dá pra entender por que o músico guardava tanto segredo sobre sua idade: o número não tem nada a ver com o sambista que tocou, com vigor, por mais de duas horas.

A gente nunca sabe como está o alquimista até que ele surge, poucas vezes por ano. Ao contrário de alguns contemporâneos, Jorge Ben faz, no máximo, meia dúzia de shows anuais. Não tem turnê de despedida, comemorativa... nem turnê, de modo geral.

Por isso, Jorge Ben deixou fãs curiosos ao anunciar um show intitulado "Alquimia Popular Brasileira". À primeira vista, muitos esperavam uma homenagem ao emblemático "A Tábua de Esmeralda" (1974). No mínimo, um show diferente dos que ele faz anualmente em São Paulo.

Não foi bem o caso: o setlist não escapou muito do padrão, só ganhou algumas adesões (como a bem-vinda "Errare Humanum Est", de "A Tábua"). A grande diferença foi a bela estrutura no palco, com dois telões cúbicos nas laterais e um telão circular atrás da banda. Nada muito exagerado nem fora do tom, mas finamente pensado pra ampliar o show.

Jorge Ben Jor se apresenta no Nubank Parque, no dia 17 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação/Lais Moss

Aliás, havia, sim, uma novidade importante: foi um show para 51 mil pessoas, segundo a assessoria. Anunciar show em estádio tem sido comum — encher, nem tanto. Principalmente para um artista nacional que, querendo ou não, veio para São Paulo no Espaço Unimed nos últimos dois anos.

Não era uma despedida nem uma celebração de data redonda, mas o clima era de homenagem a uma carreira inigualável, com o privilégio de acontecer em vida.

Desde o início, Ben Jor não deu fôlego para a plateia (nem para a banda: muitas vezes, ele parecia estar improvisando, e o grupo tentando acompanhar). Emendou sequências matadoras, como "Magnólia", "Ive Brussel", "Menina mulher da pele preta", "O telefone tocou novamente", "Oba Lá Vem Ela", "País Tropical", e a lista continua.

Tocou muito, falou pouco. Justamente por ser tão lacônico, com o olhar escondido atrás dos óculos escuros, surpreendeu todo mundo ao se emocionar. Ao fim de "Alcohol", trocou o "gosto tanto de você" por "gosto tanto de vocês" e começou a chorar, ovacionado.

Havia outros motivos para as emoções estarem à flor da pele: a 8 dias do resultado de uma eleição presidencial acirrada, o tema pairava sobre o público, mesmo sem Ben Jor se manifestar.

Quando ele incluiu "Costa do Marfim", faixa em que entoa "pega a mulher do vinte e dois / ganha a mulher do vinte e dois", parte da plateia respondeu com um coro de "Olê, olê, olá, Lula", enquanto outros fizeram gestos de 22.

Jorge Ben Jor, Simoninha, Samuel Rosa, Edi Rock, Rael, Baby do Brasil, entre outros em show no Nubank Parque, em São Paulo, em outubro de 2026 — Foto: Divulgação

Mas nem a maior polarização política do Brasil tirou o efeito desse show. Só alguém como Jorge Ben reuniria Samuel Rosa, Baby do Brasil, Rael, Edi Rock, entre outros para cantar "Taj Mahal" no palco.

De certa forma, a noite lembrou como Jorge Ben é o próprio cânone da cultura brasileira, misturando gente, suingue, futebol e simpatia. Mesmo nos tempos mais duros, ele sabe fazer festa como ninguém.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus Responds to Criticism of Hollywood Bowl Show: ‘I Am Fully Present’
articles.summary: “I can take a lot, but one thing I will not stand is any question about where my heart is when I’m on the stage”
articles.body:
Miley Cyrus addressed the criticism of her comeback show at the Hollywood Bowl on Friday night, calling out "clickbait" videos that accused her of not fully investing herself in the performance because she didn't sing every word of the songs.

"I've never heard that I don't put my heart into something," she told the audience at her second Bowl concert on Sunday night. "I don't know if any of you heard that," she said of the criticism. "That somebody was doing commentary to get clickbait on their video talking about my show on Friday night, but I'm a lot of things, and we're not even going to entertain that."

The singer, who hadn't performed live in four years prior to Friday night, added that anytime she's done something that's a steppingstone for her life or career it's been "controversial."

"And the controversy, it used to be a lot of fun," she said. "It still can be. I can be pretty melted. I love that about me. I actually used to live my life pretty hard. Because life's hard so I thought I had to get hard.… But, you know, I didn't enjoy my life as much when I was living hard. I love pouring myself into something."

"It is hard for me to stand up here and do this show," Cyrus continued. "It does not come as natural as it once did to me before. Because, like all of us, we change, we evolve, we grow, and we find what gets to come with us. What continues to fit."

She clarified that the show is not an experiment for the audience. "This is an experience for me," the singer said. "And you all make the experience possible. [This is] the only way I get to test my personal boundaries, my limits, what I think I can do."

She added, "I can take a lot, but one thing I will not stand is any question about where my heart is when I'm on the stage. Not one. I am fully present."

Cyrus also referenced the issue during her performance of recent single "Bass Persuades," noting, "Oh, I forgot, I'm supposed to sing every fucking word."

Cyrus doesn't currently have any further tour dates scheduled. Her latest album, Bass Persuades , came out in September. Rolling Stone wrote of the LP, "The fickle pop public Cyrus once wanted to appease no longer seems to no longer have any leverage over her. Through the thundering sound of Bass Persuades , she can't hear their defiant rebuttals to the notion that her audience will go where she goes. They aren't what motivates her — especially not in the way the love she goes home to at the end of the night does."

articles.title: Netizens praise Tiger Shroff for moving to driver's seat and taking him to Nanavati hospital after gun fire incident: 'This is what the real courage and bravery look like' - WATCH VIDEO
articles.summary: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff escaped without any gunshot wounds after unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai on Sunday evening.
articles.body: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff escaped without any gunshot wounds after unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai on Sunday evening. The 36-year-old actor was reportedly leaving a football club in Juhu when the incident took place. While fans were relieved that he was safe, many have also praised him for his presence of mind in rushing his injured driver to the hospital.A video that has surfaced online reportedly shows the 'Baaghi' actor moving to the driver's seat after his driver, Firdous, was injured in the shooting. Tiger is then seen driving the vehicle to Nanavati Hospital in Mumbai to ensure that his driver receives immediate medical attention. The footage has drawn considerable attention on social media, with several users praising the actor and calling him a “real-life hero”.According to media reports, three men on a motorcycle opened fire at Tiger's car as he was returning home after playing football in Juhu. One of the bullets reportedly passed through the vehicle's window, injuring Firdous. Tiger is also said to have suffered minor abrasions from gunpowder and broken glass, but escaped without any bullet injuries.Following the shooting, Tiger reportedly moved into the driver's seat and drove Firdous to Nanavati Hospital instead of waiting for assistance. His response during the emergency has since become a talking point online, with social media users commending him for prioritising his driver's safety.A report citing a senior doctor stated that initial scans revealed a foreign body lodged in Firdous's left hand following the bullet injury. Tiger, meanwhile, reportedly sustained minor abrasions.The firing took place around 300 metres from Juhu Police Station, according to The Times of India. The assailants reportedly fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station after the incident. The exact circumstances surrounding the shooting are still being investigated.As the video circulated online, several users applauded Tiger for acting swiftly after his driver was injured. One user wrote, "This is what the real courage and bravery look like"Another commented, "Amazing presence of mind by tiger shroff , after shooting incident he Did not get out of the car , shifted the driver seat inside only,"The footage has continued to attract attention, with many highlighting the actor's decision to take his injured driver to the hospital amid a potentially dangerous situation.Mumbai Police are investigating the shooting and have reportedly recorded Firdous's statement. While media reports have suggested that multiple rounds were fired at Tiger's vehicle, investigators are examining the sequence of events and the circumstances that led to the attack.The incident has also renewed discussions about security concerns surrounding celebrities, following previous threats and attacks involving personalities such as Salman Khan, Rohit Shetty, Kapil Sharma, AP Dhillon, Guru Randhawa and Gippy Grewal.Some of these incidents have been linked in media reports to threats allegedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. However, the circumstances differ from case to case, and no connection between those incidents and the firing at Tiger's car has been established. articles.title: Eric Dane reveals daughter had to save him from drowning amid ALS battle
articles.summary: In his posthumous memoir, Eric Dane reveals the reason he was let go from "Grey's Anatomy" and a near-drowning amid his ALS fight.
articles.body:
Eric Dane 's life is being detailed in a posthumous new memoir.

" My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments ," written by the late actor before his February death at 53 from Lou Gehrig's disease, is set to be released Nov. 3, 2026 (The Open Field / Penguin Publishing Group).

In an excerpt shared by People ahead of the release, Dane recalls the moment his health declined to the point where he couldn't swim. During a vacation in Antigua, his daughter Georgia and her friend have to save him from the water.

After the ordeal, he told ex Rebecca Gayheart over the phone, "I can't swim, Rebecca. I can't swim."

"She explodes into tears and I weep with her," Dane writes of his wife. "We cry together. Finally, the tears slow, become reduced to gasps, and when we're both cried out, Rebecca says, 'I was afraid of this day. I knew it would come. I've been dreading it.'"

The " Grey's Anatomy " star battled Lou Gehrig's disease, also known as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis or ALS, for less than two years before his death. While Dane and Gayheart were no longer in a relationship, the pair remained married and close coparents until the "Euphoria" actor died on Feb. 19, 2026.

From 'Grey's Anatomy' to 'Brilliant Minds,' see Eric Dane's career

Eric Dane played Dr. Mark Sloan, aka "McSteamy," on "Grey's Anatomy" for six seasons, but he's not done wooing his audiences yet. In 2025, Dane returned to TV on another medical drama, making his "Brilliant Minds" debut as "Bronx-Gen's favorite silver fox." Dane revealed in April that he’d been diagnosed with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, known as ALS . See the actor's career in the spotlight from the early 2000's to now, including here as he attends the "Countdown" premiere and afterparty on June 18, 2025, in Los Angeles.

Eric Dane reveals addiction's role in 'Grey's Anatomy' exit in memoir 'My Book of Days'

Elsewhere in the memoir, Dane reveals the reason for his exit on "Grey's." The actor details a painkiller addiction during his time on the ABC medical drama, leading series creator Shonda Rhimes to pull him aside, offering to "take care" of him if he needs time away from the series. Despite entering rehab five times over the course of the show, Dane says other factors contributed to the end of his tenure as "McSteamy."

New 'Grey's Anatomy' spinoff series set in Texas is coming

"Over time, I come out improved. I do my best. I manage my addictions, I stay sober on set," he writes, per People. "But things have changed. Look at me. Physically, I appear healthy. But mentally, I'm on my way out. I love Mark Sloan, but I need to quit him."

By 2012, toward the end of Season 8 of the series, Rhimes told the actor the show would not be bringing him back for Season 9.

"My 'Grey's Anatomy' ending does come, but not because of my addiction, although it's safe to say my addiction didn't help," Dane writes. "The reason comes down to money … Despite Mark Sloan's popularity, I have become too expensive. I have become expendable."

'Grey's Anatomy' doctors who've come and gone, including Eric Dane

Isaiah Washington (Dr. Preston Burke, Seasons 1-3): The quiet but intense cardiothoracic surgeon left fiancée Cristina Yang at the altar in the Season 3 finale. Burke went on to win a prestigious award at another hospital and later ran a private research hospital in Switzerland, which he later turned over to Yang when Oh left at the end of Season 10. He then moved to Italy with his wife and two daughters.

Penguin Random House previously confirmed Dane was able to complete "My Book of Days" before his death, which he was working on "right up to the end." It will be published on Nov. 3, in keeping with his wishes for "his daughters and readers to have these words."

"This deeply personal work is a reflection on family, resilience, faith, sobriety, fatherhood, and what it means to live fully in the face of terminal illness," the publisher said in a release. "It is both a meditation on time and a generous offering to readers about how to honor the days that matter most."

articles.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Accused allegedly conducted reccee of the actor's house, football ground, investigators are now reviewing CCTV footage from previous days
articles.summary: The men suspected of opening fire at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai had allegedly visited his residence multiple times before the incident, with
articles.body: The men suspected of opening fire at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai had allegedly visited his residence multiple times before the incident, with investigators now scrutinising CCTV footage to establish their movements. Mumbai Police sources said the accused had also visited the football ground, including on the Sunday of the shooting, as the investigation into the attack continues.According to police sources, the suspects allegedly conducted reconnaissance in pairs to avoid drawing attention to themselves. CCTV cameras outside the actor’s residence reportedly captured their movements in the area. Investigators are now reviewing footage from previous days to ascertain how frequently the men visited the property before the firing.Meanwhile, three men suspected of involvement in the attack were detained by Kota Police after officers searched the Pune–Jaipur Express at Kota railway station on Monday. The men were travelling in the general compartment and had allegedly planned to reach Nepal via Delhi, Kota Superintendent of Police Tejaswini Gautam said.The search was launched after Kota Police received an alert from their Mumbai counterparts about the suspected movement of the accused by train. Gautam said the force’s technical team was mobilised within 15 minutes of receiving the information. Officers subsequently searched the train after it arrived at Kota station at approximately 10.30 am.The three suspects were detained within around 15 minutes of the search beginning, the SP said. According to reports, two of the men are residents of Haryana, while the third belongs to Maharashtra.Gautam credited the coordination between Mumbai and Kota Police for the swift operation. No weapons were recovered from the three men when they were detained. The suspects are being questioned to establish their alleged involvement in the firing and verify details of their proposed escape route. Investigators are also probing whether they intended to travel to Delhi before crossing into Nepal.The three men have reportedly been linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. articles.title: In 2006, Al Pacino started renting Jackie Collins's Beverly Hills home for 18 years; the home was later put up on the market for USD 15.95M after he moved out in 2024
articles.summary: Al Pacino spent 18 years renting the iconic Beverly Hills home of Jackie Collins, which is now on the market for $15.95 million after his departure. Discover the luxurious amenities and rich history of this stunning property.
articles.body: Not all celebrities have a tendency to buy out properties; they prefer to rent the spaces for as long as they like. Legendary icon Al Pacino is one of them. The ‘The Godfather’ actor rented the 1922 residence, which is located in the Beverly Hills Flats, for nearly two decades. Later, it was put out on the market for USD 15.95 million. The property carries a rich history intertwined with Hollywood literature, architecture, and high-end real estate dealings.In 2006, the ‘The Godfather’ actor started renting Jackie Collins’ iconic Beverly Hills homeRather than buying his own property in the area, Al Pacino chose to set up his base in one of Jackie Collins’ iconic residences located in the posh area of the Beverly Hills neighborhood. According to an Architectural Digest report, Pacino rented the place due to the fact that members of Collins's family had previously lived there. He managed to arrange a long-term lease with her directly as his West Coast base.Jackie Collins had originally acquired the 1922 home, which was located next door to her main mansion, to serve as a private compound/guest residence. She leased it to Pacino, providing him with an established, highly secure, and screened property in the heart of the Beverly Hills Flats.Pacino stayed in the property well after Collins’ passing in 2015, and when the ownership was shifted to real estate investor Ben Nehmadi a year later. He bought the property in 2016 following the star’s passing and set up a deal to keep the Oscar-winning actor as a tenant for nearly another decade. He stayed there until shortly before the home was put up for sale in early 2025.Though the actor stayed in the property for almost two decades, the amount of rent that they paid on a monthly basis was never revealed to the public.Some of the amenities that Al Pacino’s former rented property hasSome of the amenities provided along with the 0.69-acre property included a full-sized tennis court, a swimming pool, a hot tub, and a cabana with an outdoor fireplace. The main residence itself was 5,200 square feet and featured a six-bedroom layout, along with a massive great room with wood paneling, coffered ceilings, a fireplace, a pool table, and a full wet bar.Originally, the property was built in 1922; however, over the years it underwent a lot of reconstruction and renovations. In 1938, architect Douglas Honnold was handed the project to cover the renovations on Collins’ second property. He also worked with John Lautner on the Beverly Hills Athletic Club in 1945.Al Pacino’s former residence, which once belonged to Jackie Collins, was put up on the market last yearThe house in Beverly Hills finally made its way to the market last year, a year after Pacino decided to move out. articles.title: Theranos whistleblower calls Holmes "almost unrecognizable" in film
articles.summary: Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz said he "was pretty shocked" by the version of Elizabeth Holmes he saw onscreen in the new documentary "You Can See Every...
articles.body:
Tyler Shultz, a former Theranos employee and one of the whistleblowers credited with exposing Elizabeth Holmes' now-infamous biotech company as a fraud, said he "was pretty shocked" by the version of Holmes he saw onscreen in the new documentary " You Can See Everything."

"The Elizabeth that I knew completely commanded a room, even if that room was full of secretaries of state, secretaries of defense, generals, senators. She would own a room," Shultz said Monday on "CBS Mornings." "She had so much confidence, and the woman that I saw onscreen looked, frankly, like a, a broken woman."

"It was almost unrecognizable," he added.

Shultz also said he believes Holmes misled Nathan Fielder, who directed the documentary alongside Lance Oppenheim, when at one point in the film she pulled out what she claimed was Theranos' blood-testing device.

"She brings out the Theranos device, and she lays it across the table and all of its components, so you know you can see everything," said Shultz. "But my problem was: that was not the device that I worked with 12 hours a day. That was not the device that we hid from regulators. That was not the device that failed quality controls. That was not the device that we used to knowingly give patients incorrect medical information, and she completely misled [Fielder] down this completely different rabbit hole."

Holmes never admitted wrongdoing in the wake of the Theranos scandal , a stance on which she held firm in the documentary which brings viewers inside Holmes' San Diego rental property in 2023 just weeks before the start of her 11-year prison sentence. At the time, she was living with her partner, Billy Evans, who is also featured prominently in the documentary, and their two children.

Holmes was convicted in 2022 of multiple counts of defrauding Theranos' investors, who, like the public, were led to believe that the company could conduct thorough clinical analyses on tiny blood samples pricked from a fingertip rather than drawn the traditional way. The technology was billed as revelatory for the field of diagnostics, increasing access to and costs of crucial, even life-saving, testing.

But Theranos turned out to be a sham — the technology couldn't do what it claimed. And Holmes, who had become a symbol of Silicon Valley's visionary potential, became the subject of widespread scrutiny as people wondered how she managed to deceive so many, and why she had gone to such great lengths to try to build a business on a false promise.

"She knows that she did something wrong," Shultz said on Monday. "She knows that she was lying, because she created this whole web of lies that you would not have needed to create if you actually believed the lies."

Shultz was hired in 2013 as an intern at Theranos, where his grandfather, former U.S. Secretary of State George Shultz, served as a board member. Tyler left the company the following year and went on serve as an informant for investigations into its dubious practices by The Wall Street Journal and various government regulatory agencies. He later participated in the 2016 HBO documentary "The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley," which covered Theranos' downfall.

"You Can See Everything" premiered on Friday and earned $15 million at the box office in its opening weekend, the second-most profitable opening weekend ever for a documentary.

articles.title: Miley Cyrus on the Supernatural Sign She Received from Dolly Parton: ‘I Know She’s Here with Me’
articles.summary: The singer officially ushered in her new musical era during the second of her two special Los Angeles shows on Sunday, Oct. 18
articles.body:
Miley Cyrus spoke about the supernatural sign she received from her late godmother Dolly Parton during night 2 of her Hollywood Bowl shows

The pop star also addressed criticism she faced following her night 1 performance on Friday, Oct. 16

Cyrus released her 10th studio album, Bass Persuades , on Sept. 18

Miley Cyrus shared a sweet story about Dolly Parton before performing "Jolene" during night 2 of her Hollywood Bowl show.

The singer, 33, returned to the venue for her second performance on Sunday, Oct. 18, with MODEL/ACTRIZ joining her as the special guest for both dates.

The concert comes as Miley enters a new chapter of her career with her 10th studio album, Bass Persuades , which was released on Sept. 18.

Before performing "Jolene" in honor of Parton who died on Aug. 25 at 80 , Cyrus recalled having a supernatural experience with her late godmother.

"I actually have a Dolly mannequin in my bedroom. She gave it to me for Christmas, and it's dressed like her, it's built like her, and when I was by myself I actually took my phone and I played 'Jolene' for her on video just holding it up to the mannequin and lit a candle," she recalled.

Miley continued, "And I put a flower down for her, and I said 'Dolly, if you're here right now, flicker the lights,' and I didn't say anything out loud, but the entire hallway started flickering."

The "Let's Get Married" performer said that her fiancé Maxx Morando could vouch for the experience.

"He was there, but he didn't know what I said. But I know [Dolly's] here with me tonight, and I'm feeling some of the feelings that I'm most afraid of, but having her here with me is getting me through and having you here with me is getting me through," said Miley.

She added, "So no matter what it takes, this show is for you. And for Dolly."

Miley was also crying as she held a framed picture of Dolly and encouraged the audience to sing along to "Used to Be Young." "Let my Aunt Dolly hear you," she told the crowd.

During the Friday, Oct. 16 show at the Hollywood Bowl, Miley also paid tribute to the country legend with an emotional performance of "Jolene" after crying on stage.

The "Walk of Fame" artist also addressed criticism of Friday's concert, before singing "Something Beautiful."

"I pride myself on being soft and strong at the same time," Miley began. "That's something I love about me is that I can be vulnerable. I have never heard that I don't put my heart into something."

She then addressed a fan sharing commentary "to get clickbait on their video" about her Oct. 16 performance.

"I'm a lot of things, and we're not even going to entertain that because you all have been with me long enough to know that any time I'm doing something meaningful that's going to be a stepping stone in my life, in my career, to propel me forward to not only be the artist, but the person that I want to be," said Miley.

She recalled how she "used to live my life pretty hard because life's hard so I thought that I had to get hard."

"But you know I didn't enjoy my life as much when I was living hard," she added. "I love pouring myself into something, and I'll be honest, what I said, don't mince the words, because it is hard for me to stand up here and do this show. It does not come as natural as it once did to me before."

Miley noted that it's because "we change, we evolve, we grow."

"You all are more to me than an experiment," she told the fans. "That is absolutely not what this is. This is not an experiment of you, this is an experience for me. And you all make the experience possible."

Miley then said that before she performed "Orbit" that night, she "had already told myself I wasn't going to come on stage."

"I was going to run away, but never would I leave you all sitting in these seats unfulfilled from a show, so I can take a lot but one thing I will not stand is any question about where my heart is when I'm on this stage. Not one," she said.

Added Miley, "I'm fully present; every bit of our fears, they live in the future, and I have no business even questioning that right now because the only thing that I have is this moment with all of you.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

"To make it clear, I am all here with you right now. Nowhere else I'd rather be," she concluded.

During the encore, Miley and Morando, 27, walked out hand in hand before performing "Let's Get Married."

Closing out the night, the Hannah Montana star changed one line of the lyrics from "Flowers" to say, "Sorry to cry but then remember I sold out the Hollywood Bowl twice"

Beyond the performances, the Hollywood Bowl shows mark another milestone in Cyrus' evolving relationship with her music and public persona. With Bass Persuades , she is also embracing a simpler approach to her name, releasing the project under just Miley .

Billy Ray Cyrus also celebrated his daughter's new chapter. Following Miley's album announcement, the country singer, 65, shared a throwback photo of himself with Miley and her younger brother, Braison Cyrus , and praised her decision to go by just her first name, likening the move to other music legends.

"I mentioned Dolly and Cher . Thinkin about it more and more … Elvis .. Prince …and so on," he wrote on Instagram . "It's a natural progression for an iconic superstar legend. And the legend continues ! Looking forward to the new album."

When Miley announced Bass Persuades , she also shared what the album's title and the project as a whole mean to her.

"Music takes hold of us. We feel it, sing it, sometimes dance to it, let it out and carry on. It is powerful, vulnerable, sweet and strong," she wrote on Instagram . "Heart full, heartache, every part of life in between. That's what the title means to me. Thank you for being a part of making my wildest dreams come true. I sincerely hope you love this album. ❤️ Miley."

articles.title: Luke Bryan Reveals Son Bo, 18, Is Heading Into Surgery After Getting Injured During High School Football Game
articles.summary: The country singer’s son was injured during a high school football game on Friday, Oct. 16
articles.body:
Luke Bryan's son Bo is heading into surgery

The teenager broke his collarbone after being tackled during a football game on Friday, Oct. 16

The country singer shares his two sons with wife Caroline

Luke Bryan's son is heading into surgery.

The country singer, 50, shared on Instagram on Monday, Oct. 19, that his 18-year-old son Thomas "Bo" Boyer would be undergoing surgery after he was injured during a high school football game. In a video shared on his Instagram, Bryan was in the car with his son and his wife Caroline as they drove to Bo's surgery.

"Well, it's us. Going for surgery," Bryan said in the short clip, panning to show his son sitting next to him in a sling. Bryan's wife Caroline appeared behind the musician, asking who Bryan was talking to.

Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE's free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories.

Caroline also shared a snap on her Instagram of Bo wearing a hospital gown ahead of his surgery. In the picture, the country singer makes a silly face as he stands beside Bo and Caroline in an exam room.

"Not the best day for Bo, or our family, but he'll be back!!!! Dang collarbone…and of course Luke can't take a serious picture!" she captioned her post.

On Friday, Oct. 16, the 18-year-old was sacked during the Battle Ground Academy game against Pope John Paul II High School, according to The Tennessean .

The outlet reported that Bo hit the ground and landed on his right shoulder, and medics and trainers opted to put his arm in a sling and kept his shoulder wrapped as he sat on the sidelines for the rest of the game.

The following day, the teenage quarterback confirmed that he had broken his collarbone via his Instagram Stories, per USA Today . "Broke my collarbone last night," he wrote. "Thank you everyone for your thoughts and prayers. We will be back."

The "Country Girl" singer and his wife Caroline share two sons: Bo and Tatum "Tate" Christopher, born in 2010. Along with his two sons, Bryan and Caroline took in the country singer's nephew Til and nieces Jordan and Kris after the deaths of their mother, Bryan's sister Kelly, in 2007, and their father, Ben Cheshire, seven years later.

Bo — who is the starting quarterback and is considered one of the top high school quarterbacks in the region with 2,006 yards passing, 30 touchdowns and three interceptions to date — said that two players landed on him after the sack as he spoke with reporters after the game.

"I thought it was just a stinger when I hit the ground," he explained. "Once I got up I knew something was wrong. When I got to the sideline, I really knew something was wrong."

"I don't know what we're looking at yet," BGA coach Bobby Bentley told The Tennessean . "We'll have to figure this thing out. That's the challenge for us as a team and as coaches. What do we do? How do we do it? We're going to figure it out."

articles.title: In 2015, Jay-Z bought Tidal for $56 million; six years later, the rapper sold a majority stake to Jack Dorsey’s Square in a $297 million deal
articles.summary: Rapper and entrepreneur Jay-Z made a major move in the music streaming industry in 2015 when he joined a group of prominent artists to acquire Tidal, a
articles.body: Rapper and entrepreneur Jay-Z made a major move in the music streaming industry in 2015 when he joined a group of prominent artists to acquire Tidal, a Norwegian music streaming service. The deal, valued at approximately $56 million, reflected his ambition to build a platform that gave musicians a greater role in the business behind their music. Six years later, Tidal entered a new chapter when Jack Dorsey’s financial technology company, Square, agreed to acquire a majority stake in the service for $297 million.Jay-Z acquired Tidal in 2015 for $56 millionIn January 2015, a company controlled by Jay-Z, operating through Project Panther Bidco, made an offer to acquire Aspiro, the Norwegian technology company behind the streaming services Tidal and WiMP. The offer was valued at approximately $56 million.The acquisition was completed in March 2015, paving the way for Tidal to develop under new ownership. Jay-Z subsequently relaunched the service with a group of internationally recognised musicians, positioning it as an artist-led alternative in the increasingly competitive music streaming market.The group of artist co-owners included Beyoncé, Alicia Keys, Rihanna, Madonna, Usher, Nicki Minaj and Chris Martin of Coldplay, among others. Their involvement helped distinguish Tidal from competing services by placing established musicians at the centre of its identity.Tidal entered the market with an emphasis on high-quality audio, exclusive content and a closer connection between musicians and their audiences. Its ownership structure also reflected an ambition to give artists a direct stake in the platform through which their work reached listeners. Tidal continued to operate in this competitive environment while developing its own identity and services.Jack Dorsey’s Square announced a $297 million deal in 2021On March 4, 2021, Square announced that it had reached an agreement to acquire a significant majority ownership stake in Tidal. The company said it expected to pay $297 million through a combination of cash and stock.Square, co-founded and led by Jack Dorsey at the time, was primarily known for its payment-processing and financial technology services. Its interest in Tidal represented an expansion into the music industry, with a particular focus on providing artists with financial tools and new ways to generate income.Under the proposed arrangement, Tidal would continue operating independently within Square’s business ecosystem. Its existing artist shareholders would retain minority ownership rather than surrendering all their interests in the platform.The announcement also confirmed that Jay-Z was expected to join Square’s board of directors following the completion of the transaction.Jay-Z remained involved after the saleThe agreement did not mark Jay-Z’s complete departure from Tidal. Instead, it changed the company’s ownership structure while allowing him and other artist shareholders to retain an interest in the business.The transaction was completed on April 30, 2021. According to Square’s subsequent regulatory filing, the company acquired an 86.8% ownership interest in Tidal.The final transaction consideration differed from the initially announced $297 million figure. Square’s regulatory filings reported approximately $302 million in consideration for the acquisition, subject to adjustments and including specified outstanding indebtedness, transaction expenses and other amounts. The company’s later financial reporting also separately recorded the acquisition’s accounting value.From a $56 million acquisition to a major technology partnershipThe two transactions marked different stages in Tidal’s development. The 2015 acquisition brought the streaming service under Jay-Z’s ownership, with support from a group of prominent musicians. The 2021 deal placed majority ownership in the hands of a financial technology company looking to expand its services for artists.The figures associated with the deals also illustrate the scale of the change: an acquisition valued at approximately $56 million in 2015 was followed six years later by a majority-stake transaction initially announced at $297 million.However, the amounts represent different transactions and should not be treated as a straightforward calculation of Tidal’s increase in value. For Jay-Z, the transaction was another example of his involvement in business ventures beyond music. For Tidal, it introduced a new majority owner while preserving a role for its artist shareholders.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Andy opina sobre la nueva nariz de Lucas: "Está incluso mejor que antes"
articles.standfirst: El cantante asegura que la salud de su antiguo compañero es lo más importante, aunque reconoce que intenta mantenerse al margen de su vida personal tras la ruptura del dúo
articles.summary: El cantante asegura que la salud de su antiguo compañero es lo más importante, aunque reconoce que intenta mantenerse al margen de su vida personal tras la ruptura del dúo
articles.body: Andy Morales se ha pronunciado sobre el aspecto actual de Lucas, su antiguo compañero musical, después de la intervención quirúrgica a la que este se sometió para reconstruir su nariz. El cantante ha valorado positivamente el resultado, aunque ha aclarado que solo ha visto algunas imágenes y que prefiere mantenerse al margen de todo lo relacionado con su expareja artística. "De verdad que no lo he visto. Solamente he visto imágenes, que la salud, como dije yo, es lo principal. He visto que está bien. Incluso mejor que antes", ha explicado en declaraciones a Europa Press. Sus palabras llegan aproximadamente un año después de que ambos artistas pusieran fin a su trayectoria conjunta, tras dos décadas de carrera y éxitos musicales. Desde entonces, los dos han continuado sus caminos por separado, sin que sus últimas declaraciones apunten a una posible reconciliación personal o profesional. El artista ha insistido en que no quiere participar en comentarios ni polémicas relacionadas con la vida de Lucas. "No he visto más, de verdad, porque intento no entrar en ninguna más, ninguna historia porque al final creo que no me beneficia, al contrario", ha declarado Andy. Andy ha querido dejar claro que respeta las decisiones de su antiguo compañero y que no considera oportuno pronunciarse más allá de lo que ha visto. "Es la vida de cada uno y yo no puedo entrar ahí", ha sentrenciado. Al margen de esta cuestión, Andy se ha mostrado satisfecho con su presente profesional y con los proyectos que prepara como solista. "Estoy muy contento, estoy terminando el año, la verdad, que maravilloso. Tengo proyectos muy bonitos y no puedo pedirle más a la música", ha afirmado. También ha reconocido que mantenerse en la industria musical no es sencillo debido a la competencia, aunque considera que atraviesa una buena etapa. "Yo no me puedo quejar. Tengo muchísima suerte", ha subrayado Andy. La nariz de Lucas ha acaparado la atención mediática después de que tuviera que someterse a una nueva operación a finales de agosto para reconstruirla. La intervención llegó después de una primera cirugía, realizada en octubre de 2024, cuyo resultado no fue el esperado y que le provocó problemas que hicieron necesaria una reparación posterior. El artista mostró públicamente su nueva imagen en '¡De viernes!', programa de Telecinco, el pasado mes de septiembre. Durante la entrevista, Lucas se mostró satisfecho con el resultado de la reconstrucción: "Me ha quedado de maravilla, no paro de mirarme al espejo", manifestó. Desde entonces, el aspecto de Lucas ha generado numerosos comentarios, entre ellos el de su excompañero Andy, que ha optado por valorar favorablemente el resultado sin entrar en detalles sobre la intervención ni sobre la relación que mantiene actualmente con su antiguo compañero.

articles.title: Daler Mehndi asked to stop singing at Navratri event in Tehri: 'There is a Durga Mata programme for Navratri, and you are singing at the event after drinking alcohol'
articles.summary: A performance by Punjabi singer Daler Mehndi at an event in Uttarakhand has landed in controversy after state cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal went on stage
articles.body: A performance by Punjabi singer Daler Mehndi at an event in Uttarakhand has landed in controversy after state cabinet minister Subodh Uniyal went on stage and asked him to stop singing. A video of the incident has since gone viral on social media.What happened at Kunjapuri fairDaler Mehndi was performing on Sunday at the Kunjapuri Fair in Uttarakhand’s Tehri district. The cultural programme was part of the Navratri celebrations. Subodh Uniyal, who is also the MLA for Narendranagar, objected to the performance and walked onto the stage.Subodh Uniyal told the singer that the event was dedicated to the worship of Goddess Durga and that performing under the influence of alcohol was not appropriate. Standing right next to the singer, he said, “There is a Durga Mata programme for Navratri, and you are singing at the event after drinking alcohol, which is not appropriate.”The minister added that the religious nature of the celebrations required performers to respect the occasion’s dignity and decorum. The Kunjapuri Fair is an important religious and cultural gathering in the region.'You are making a fool of us'Subodh Uniyal also spoke about why the singer had been invited. “We called you so that our people could be entertained. You are making a fool of us,” he said. “This is wrong. It’s wrong. You have a big name; we should respect that. You were called because you have a big name.”Daler Mehndi’s response in the videoIn the clip, Daler Mehndi appeared to interrupt the minister. He said, “Sir, I request you with folded hands...please leave the stage."The singer has not yet responded to the incident and allegations as of now.Disclaimer: We have not independently verified whether the singer was under the influence of alcohol. articles.title: Late Hulk Hogan’s daughter Brooke Hogan reveals painful rift with her father; claims brother Nick has ‘ghosted’ her
articles.summary: In a candid interview, Brooke Hogan discusses the familial rift with her late father, Hulk Hogan, and the ongoing tension with her brother Nick following their father's death. Revealing deep-seated issues, Brooke emphasizes how their public image contrasts with their private struggles.
articles.body: Brooke Hogan's relationship with her father, Hulk Hogan, was complicated long before his death. But more than a year after losing the wrestling legend, Brooke says the family tensions have not gone away. In a new interview, she spoke about her estrangement from her late father, her fractured relationship with brother Nick Hogan and why the family's happy image on television never showed the full picture.In an exclusive report published by RadarOnline on Monday, October 19, 2026, Brooke opened up about the family rift that continued after Hulk passed away at 71 on July 24, 2025. She said the family's public image was very different from what she experienced privately.“My family's narrative has always been like, 'Oh, we're so happy for Brooke. We're so proud of Brooke.' But it's really hard to see that same stock response when the reality behind closed doors is extremely different,” she said.For viewers who grew up watching 'Hogan Knows Best', the comments offer a very different picture of the family they saw on screen.Brooke Hogan says brother Nick has 'ghosted' herOne of the most painful parts of the fallout, according to Brooke Hogan, has been her relationship with Nick. She said they have barely spoken since their father's death, despite Nick publicly presenting the family as being on good terms.Brooke recalled asking Nick for a particular cross that Hulk used to wear. Instead, she said, she received two cross necklaces she did not recognise. “Since Dad's death, my brother has ghosted us while publicly embracing his position as the keeper of Dad's legacy, all while saying we're 'in a great place.' We don't even talk,” she said.She also said she would have handled things differently if their positions had been reversed. “Had our positions been reversed, I know how generous I planned to be with him. That's what hurts,” Brooke added.She was keen to make one thing clear: the disagreement was not simply about who received which belongings. “The belongings aren't what ruptured the relationship; it was everything surrounding them,” she said.Nick's perspective on the latest claims was not included in the report, so Brooke's account should be understood as her side of the family dispute.What happened to Hulk Hogan's will?The family's estate dispute has also attracted attention, but the timeline needs some context. The outlet's October 2026 report said Brooke was excluded from her father's will, with Nick named as the sole beneficiary of an estate reportedly worth more than $5 million.However, Brooke had already explained in August 2025 that she wanted to remove herself from the will because she feared that money could trigger further conflict within the family.In an interview on 'Bubba the Love Sponge' on August 5, 2025, she described being worried about the arguments that might follow her father's death. She said she wanted to avoid being drawn into disputes involving her mother, Linda Hogan, and people in her father's circle.Separately, Us Weekly reported on September 10, 2025, that it had obtained Hulk's will and amendments. The final amendment, dated July 28, 2023, excluded Brooke and her descendants as beneficiaries.The distinction is important: Brooke's exclusion was documented, but she had also publicly said she requested to be removed. articles.summary: Matthew McConaughey's video urging Americans to rethink the two-party system drew fierce social media backlash ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.
articles.body: Matthew McConaughey's call to rethink America's two-party political system has sparked a heated debate on social media, with some critics accusing the Oscar-winning actor of promoting a "privileged perspective" ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. On Sunday, McConaughey took to social media and challenged the long-held notion that voting for an independent candidate is a wasted vote, arguing that just a handful of independent lawmakers could dramatically shift the balance of power in Washington. "They've been telling us for years that an independent vote is a wasted vote," McConaughey said in a video shared on Instagram. "Well, a great question for our times is, has that unwasted vote been working out for you?" MATTHEW MCCONAUGHEY HINTS AT POLITICAL AMBITIONS AFTER MEETING WITH POPE LEO XIV IN VATICAN CITY While the actor insisted he was not endorsing a particular candidate or political party, his message quickly drew criticism from social media users who questioned the timing of his remarks and warned against encouraging independent voting ahead of November's elections. "This message is so irresponsible right now. Do the math. Willie Nelson would not be impressed," one user commented. Another accused the Hollywood star of being out of touch with the challenges facing everyday Americans. "I understand that you're in a tax bracket where government decisions don't affect you like it does majority of constituents, but this isn't the time my guy," the user wrote. "Our government is doing their damnest to silence the lower and middle classes. These are incredibly dangerous times and we've got to get this administration OUT." A third critic slammed McConaughey's message as "ridiculous," arguing that his celebrity status and financial security bar him from facing the consequences of political decisions. "This is a ridiculous, privileged perspective from someone with nothing to lose either way," the commenter wrote. "Both sides absolutely have faults but one is dragging us deeper into cruel chaos, a broken economy, abducting our neighbors off the street, enforcing violence on its own citizens, stripping women of rights, trying actively to take away this vote you're encouraging people to utilize," the user continued. "If you're gonna hop on instagram with your quick hot take this close to a crucial election period, at least say something substantive and try to stand on the correct side." Despite the backlash, others rushed to McConaughey's defense, praising the actor for challenging political divisions and encouraging Americans to consider alternatives to the two major parties. articles.title: Richard Riehle, character actor best known for ‘Office Space,’ dies at 78
articles.summary: Richard Riehle, best known for his supporting role in Mike Judge’s corporate satire “Office Space” as Tom Smykowski, has died.
articles.body: Richard Riehle, a prolific character actor whose bushy mustache and knack for portraying beleaguered middlemen made him a favorite of Hollywood casting directors for decades, has died, his representatives said Monday. He was 78. Riehle’s representatives said he died over the weekend but did not provide details about the cause. Riehle was best known for his supporting role in Mike Judge’s corporate satire “Office Space” as Tom Smykowski, an anxious product manager who rages against the prospect of getting laid off. (“I have people skills! I am good at dealing with people! Can’t you understand that?”). He left an impression even with scant screen time, whether playing a racist quartermaster in “Glory,” a guard who allows Harrison Ford to flee in “The Fugitive,” a mob banker who gets cursed out by Joe Pesci in Martin Scorsese’s “Casino,” or a kindly auto mechanic who helps out Kristen Wiig in “Bridesmaids.” Riehle’s hundreds of credits include scores of TV roles, such as Principal Ed Rooney on the short-lived sitcom “Ferris Bueller,” a gruff grandfather on “Grounded for Life” and a police officer on “The West Wing.” He most recently appeared as a prison warden on HBO’s dark comedy “Barry.” “Beyond his immense talent, he will be remembered for his genuine goodness, boundless kindness, and unwavering generosity, particularly toward emerging actors and filmmakers, whom he encouraged and supported at every opportunity,” his talent agency and management company said in a statement. “Grounded for Life” star Donal Logue paid tribute to Riehle on Facebook, describing his co-star as “an amazing human being” and a “consummate professional.” “He was an actor’s actor — humble, kind, and incredible at his craft,” Logue wrote. “I had to apologize to him after his final network audition for ‘Grounded’ because he made me laugh so hard, I broke character and fell to the floor.” Riehle made his screen acting debut as an unnamed bartender in the 1977 road-trip movie “Joyride,” the first of more than 400 credits across film and television. Richard Mathias Riehle was born on May 12, 1948, in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin. He attended the University of Notre Dame, where he joined the campus theatrical group and grew fond of stage acting. “I always wanted the role that would bring something out of me, force me to find something extra,” Riehle told Notre Dame Magazine for the winter 2011-2012 issue. “The lead isn’t always the best part in a play or a movie.”

articles.summary: Amanda Seyfried faces backlash after appearing in "You Can See Everything" documentary, where her shifting sympathy for Elizabeth Holmes sparked debate.
articles.body: Amanda Seyfried landed in the hot seat after her appearance in the latest Elizabeth Holmes documentary unleashed a wave of criticism online. Seyfried surprised viewers when she appeared alongside Nathan Fielder in "You Can See Everything," a documentary that followed Holmes in the last 34 days leading up to the start of her prison sentence. Holmes reported to Federal Prison Camp Bryan on May 30, 2023. Seyfried revisited her connection to the disgraced Theranos founder, whom she portrayed in Hulu's "The Dropout." The new documentary, released Oct. 16, explored Seyfried's evolving perspective on Holmes, including her reactions to Holmes' personal life and relationship with Billy Evans. Stepping back into Holmes' shoes for the documentary, Seyfried helped Fielder recreate conversations he had with the disgraced Theranos founder after she reported to prison. Throughout the film, Seyfried grappled with her growing sympathy for Holmes, even as the convicted fraudster challenged the way the actress portrayed her in the Hulu series. 'YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING' REVIEW: THE BUZZY ELIZABETH HOLMES DOCUMENTARY IS WORTH THE HYPE "Amanda Seyfried defending Holmes as a victim of male manipulation until Holmes accused her of participating in a sensationalized version of the Theranos scandal and then flipping out about how it is just TV was a [sic] truly gross," one X user wrote. "I hope she gets redragged for it." Other viewers piled on, accusing Seyfried of changing her tune when the scrutiny shifted toward her own role in bringing the Theranos scandal to television. "Lots of 'women protecting women' posturing from her until she gets accused of perhaps also causing Elizabeth some degree of pain, after which she immediately deflects and starts engaging in female emotional manipulation by accusing Nathan of covering up for Elizabeth based on her 'intuition,'" another user said. "It reminds me why we should never take people like her seriously." Not everyone agreed with the harsh criticism. "imagine walking away from this blaming amanda seyfried," a user wrote. Holmes was convicted in January 2022 on four federal fraud charges for misleading investors about her blood-testing company's technology and capabilities.
